title: Fetch-Execute Cycle
body:
Fetches the *next* instruction to be executed

The loop a [[CPU]] never leaves:

1. **Fetch.** Read the instruction at the program counter from memory over the
   [[System Bus]]
2. **Decode.** Work out what it is and where its operands are ([[Addressing Modes]])
3. **Execute.** Do it, usually in the [[ALU]], and write the result back
4. Advance the program counter and go to 1

Between step 4 and step 1 is the only place an interrupt is taken. That is why an
[[IRQs|IRQ]] arriving mid-instruction waits: the instruction finishes, *then* the detour
happens. See [[Interrupts]].

The control logic driving this cycle is a [[Finite State Machine]], with the steps above as
its states. Splitting them across separate hardware so several instructions are in
different stages at once is pipelining.
